coverage.forecast_workbook: Dec-25–Dec-31 (includes some historical quarters, then estimates/forecasts/projections)
coverage.commodities: REQ commodity groups, not HS/ANZSIC: resources (aluminium, bauxite, alumina, copper, diamonds/gemstones, gold, iron ore, lead, lithium, nickel, silver, steel, tin, zinc, titanium, zircon, other resources) and energy (metallurgical coal, thermal coal, crude oil/refinery feedstock, LPG, refinery products, LNG, other energy), plus published totals.

examples: Crude oil and other refinery feedstock
commodity_classification.mapping_note: The model can store the REQ commodity_name but has no commodity_code for these groups; joins to ABS HS-level goods or OECD HS4 margins are not possible without a crosswalk.

measures.description: Quarterly commodity exports, by value (fob), Australia.
measures.actual_estimate_forecast: Historical/actual, ABS-derived; latest period preliminary; some rows marked s=estimate.
measures.notes: Components and published totals are both present. Do not add totals to components; do not add to ABS values.

measures.unit: $m for value; quantities in kt/ML/'000 ct.
measures.notes: Import valuation basis (customs value/FOB vs CIF) is not stated in the workbook; must be confirmed before treating it as FOB or CIF.

measures.description: Quarterly commodity exports, by volume, Australia.
measures.unit: Mt, kt, t, ML, LCE kt, '000 ct (varies by commodity).
measures.notes: Volumes are not dollars; units differ by commodity and table. The model has no volume_unit field.

measures.description: Export unit value index (export values divided by volumes).
measures.actual_estimate_forecast: Historical/derived index, not a spot price.
measures.notes: Despite the title 'export unit values', Table 18 is an index (base September 2026 = 100), not US$/t. Do not treat it as a price.

measures.table: Forecast workbook (Quarterly export values, Quarterly prices, Quarterly export volumes)
measures.description: Forecast/projection values, volumes and spot prices for Australian resources and energy exports.
measures.unit: $m for values; Mt/kt/t/ML/LCE kt for volumes; US$/t, US$/bbl, US$/MMBtu for spot prices.
measures.actual_estimate_forecast: Estimate/forecast/projection. Never treat f/z as actual.
measures.notes: The forecast workbook includes some historical quarters; use the historical workbook for actuals. Forecasts are a different vintage and are revised.

measures.description: No CIF/FOB margin is published; OECD ITIC remains the only margin source.

units.values: $m = millions of Australian dollars. Exports are explicitly FOB. Import valuation basis is not stated.
units.volumes: Mt (million tonnes), kt (thousand tonnes), t (tonnes), ML (megalitres), LCE kt (lithium carbonate equivalent), '000 ct (thousand carats); varies by commodity.
units.prices: Forecast workbook spot prices: US$/t, US$/bbl, US$/MMBtu; not AUD trade values. Historical Table 18 is an index (base September 2026 = 100), not a price.
units.periods: Quarterly tables are calendar quarters (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec). Annual tables are Australian financial years (1989–90 etc.). The model's financial_year/time_period semantics must not mix these.
units.no_unit_inference: Do not infer an import basis, a commodity unit, or a price currency from a bare number; the workbook has explicit unit columns for most rows and the PDF notes define the exceptions.

actual_estimate_forecast.historical_workbook: Actual/ABS-derived historical data; latest period is preliminary; some rows are marked s=estimate.
actual_estimate_forecast.forecast_workbook: s=estimate, f=forecast, z=projection; forecast values are not actuals and are revised between releases.
actual_estimate_forecast.pdf: The report contains both historical discussion and forecasts; the executive summary's 2026–27/2027–28 numbers are forecasts.
actual_estimate_forecast.rule: Never treat an f or z value as an actual. Never mix a forecast vintage with a historical actual series.

sample_values.note: XLSX values are unrounded $m; latest historical quarter is preliminary.

abs_international_trade.relationship: The REQ historical trade tables explicitly cite ABS International Trade in Goods and Services, Australia, Cat. No. 5368.0, and are ABS-derived commodity aggregates. They are not an independent source and are not additive with ABS. The current trade API summary groups by measure_type/trade_flow and sums amount_cents across sources, so ingesting REQ trade_value rows alongside ABS would double-count in the summary.
abs_international_trade.action: Do not ingest REQ trade values as an additive second source. If used, label as ABS-derived/non-additive and add a source/overlap guard in the API summary.

oecd_itic.relationship: OECD ITIC publishes CIF/FOB margins as a percentage of CIF import value. REQ publishes FOB export values and import values; no CIF/FOB margin. Different measures. Do not derive a margin by combining REQ exports and imports; that would be a cross-source derivation.
oecd_itic.action: Keep separate measure groups; never derive or add a CIF/FOB margin from REQ.

within_req.totals_vs_components: Tables 16/17/19 include published totals (Total resources, Total energy, Total resources and energy, Total merchandise, Total goods and services) alongside commodity components. Never sum totals with components.
within_req.forecast_vs_actual: Forecast workbook values are not actuals; never mix forecast vintages with historical actuals.
within_req.volumes_vs_values: Volumes (Mt/kt/t/ML) are not dollars; never add volumes to values.
within_req.prices_vs_values: Table 18 is an export unit value index, not a price; forecast spot prices are USD, not AUD trade values. Never mix them with values.

fields.trade_flow: export for Table 17; import for Table 19
fields.commodity_name: REQ commodity label (e.g. Iron ore, LNG, Metallurgical coal)
fields.commodity_code: undefined (REQ custom group; no HS code)
fields.financial_year: calendar year for quarterly rows (e.g. 2026); financial-year label for annual FY rows (e.g. 2025-26)
fields.time_period: 2026Q2 for quarterly rows; 2025-26 for annual FY rows
fields.data_quality_flag: provisional for historical ABS-derived rows (latest period preliminary); estimated for rows marked s=estimate

candidate_rows.blocker: No volume_unit field; units vary by commodity/table.

fields.price: not usable as a single column without currency/unit

candidate_rows.blocker: No price_unit/currency/index_base field; forecasts need a forecast flag.

blockers: Cross-source additivity: the current /api/v1/trade/summary groups by measure_type/trade_flow and sums amount_cents across all sources; REQ trade_value rows would double-count with ABS.
No aggregation_role/is_total field: REQ tables include published totals alongside commodity components; ingesting both would double-count within REQ.
No forecast flag/vintage: f/z forecasts and s estimates cannot be distinguished from actuals except by estimated/provisional; forecasts need a separate flag and release vintage.
No volume_unit/price_unit/currency/index_base: volumes and prices cannot be represented unambiguously.
No HS/REQ commodity code: commodity_name only; joins to ABS HS-level goods or OECD HS4 margins are not possible.
Import value basis is unstated (customs/FOB vs CIF); resolve before treating imports as FOB or CIF.
Quarterly calendar periods and annual financial-year periods are mixed in the same workbook; the model's financial_year/time_period semantics must not mix them.
The XLSX About sheets say Vol. 13 while the PDF says Vol. 15; use the PDF/release page as authoritative.
schema_changes_required: Add a source/overlap group (e.g. abs-itgs-5368) and group the trade summary by it, or exclude derived sources from ABS-inclusive sums.
Add aggregation_role/is_total so published totals are not summed with components.
Add volume_unit, price_unit, currency and index_base fields.
Add or crosswalk a commodity code/classification for REQ groups.
mapping_proposal.recommended_action: DEFER a trade-value builder in the current schema. The data are defensible (historical FOB export values and import values, 1990Q1–2026Q2), but the current trade API would double-count REQ trade_value rows with ABS and would sum REQ totals with components. If the product wants a REQ commodity-aggregate view, first add a source/overlap guard, an aggregation_role, a forecast flag and unit fields; then build a bounded connector for historical Tables 17/19 only. Otherwise use ABS for trade values and treat REQ as context/forecast material.
deferral_conditions: If the product requires a single additive national trade total across ABS + REQ, defer: the source is ABS-derived and the current API would double-count.
If the product requires forecasts as actuals, defer: f/z values are not actuals and the schema has no forecast flag/vintage.
If the product requires HS-level commodity mapping or partner-country values, defer: REQ uses custom commodity groups and national totals.
If the import valuation basis cannot be confirmed, defer the import-value series; exports are explicitly FOB and can be considered separately.
If the trade API summary is not changed to separate sources and totals, defer.

premise.statement: DISR REQ publishes accessible quarterly Australian resources/energy trade values with a usable licence and a defensible period/commodity mapping.
premise.finding: The source does publish accessible quarterly FOB export values and import values for 1990Q1–2026Q2, with a CC BY 4.0 licence and a clear REQ commodity/period structure. It is ABS-derived, contains published totals and forecasts, and uses custom commodity groups. The current trade API/schema cannot ingest it safely alongside ABS without double-counting.
premise.falsifier: If the required output is a single additive national trade total, an HS-level or partner-level series, or a forecast treated as an actual, the premise fails. In that case defer; do not invent a value series or derive a margin.
